s: A global retailer runs workloads in VPCs in six AWS Regions and connects 40 branch offices by using Site-to-Site VPN. The network team manages a transit gateway in each Region, inter-Region transit gateway peering, and static routes on every peering attachment. The company wants to isolate production, development, and shared-services traffic globally while allowing both production and development to reach shared services. The company wants to define the entire global network in one central policy and have routes propagate automatically between Regions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Keep a transit gateway in each Region. Create separate transit gateway route tables for production, development, and shared services, and use AWS Lambda functions triggered by Amazon EventBridge to update static routes on the inter-Region peering attachments.
Replace the transit gateways with a full mesh of inter-Region VPC peering connections, and use security groups that reference CIDR ranges to separate production from development.

Deploy AWS Cloud WAN with a core network policy that defines production, development, and shared-services segments across the six Regions. Use attachment policies to map VPC and VPN attachments to segments based on tags, and share the shared-services segment with the production and development segments.
Deploy a transit VPC in each Region with third-party SD-WAN virtual appliances on Amazon EC2, and run BGP between the appliances to exchange routes between Regions and segments.

w.y: AWS Cloud WAN is built for a global network defined by one core network policy: segments give global isolation, segment sharing lets production and development reach shared services, and routes propagate automatically between Regions. That removes the per-Region transit gateways and static peering routes, giving the LEAST operational overhead.

o.A: Transit gateway peering still needs static routes; adding custom Lambda automation increases, not reduces, overhead and there is no single central policy.
o.B: Peering is non-transitive, cannot terminate branch VPNs and a full mesh across many VPCs is unmanageable.
o.C: Correct: Cloud WAN segments, tag-based attachment policies and segment sharing in one central policy with dynamic inter-Region routing.
o.D: Self-managed appliances add patching, scaling and HA work; a managed global network service is available.
